section: one function against unit tests: humaneval, mbpp and pass@k
text: Drawing exactly k samples per problem and checking gives a noisy answer, so the Codex paper draws n ≥ k samples (it used n = 200, k ≤ 100), counts the c that pass, and estimates pass@k = E problems [ 1 − C(n−c, k) / C(n, k) ] n samples drawn per problem; c of them pass every test C(a, b) binomial coefficient: the number of ways to choose b of a C(n−c, k)/C(n, k) the chance that k samples drawn without replacement from the n are all failures The tempting shortcut is to estimate pass@1 as p̂ = c/n and plug it into 1 − (1 − p̂) k .
label: core
